files.description: Bike-share trips, 1 September to 1 November 2025 (1500 rows): trip_id (whole number), rider_id (refers to riders.csv), start_station and end_station (refer to station_code in stations.csv), started_at (timestamp written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM), duration_min (whole minutes; about 3% empty), distance_km (two decimals), fare (two decimals; about 3% empty), payment (card, app or cash; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), rating (1-5 stars, whole number; about 19% empty).

task_text: From trips.csv, compute the total of the distance_km column, the number of rows, and the total distance_km for each rider_id. `result` should be a dict with the keys "total", "row_count" and "per_rider", where "per_rider" holds one total per rider_id.
intended_computation: Read trips.csv; total = sum of distance_km (no empty cells); row_count = 1500; per_rider = sum of distance_km per rider_id (389 rider ids); dict with keys total, row_count, per_rider.

acceptable_variants.notes: id columns (rider_id, station codes) may be written as integers without leading zeros; per_rider may be a Series, dict or table; totals may differ in the last digits by summation order

intent_summary: From one table, compute the total of an amount column, the number of rows, and the total amount per identifier.

column_map.file choice: riders.csv skipped: each rider_id occurs once there, so totals per identifier would be the values themselves (degenerate)
